title: Clearline vs DealerSocket CRM: which fits your dealership?
summary: Compare our CRM with DealerSocket across customer records, pipelines, tasks, AI, desking, equity tools and exact integration requirements.
body_markdown:
Compare our CRM with DealerSocket by the customer work and retail requirements your store needs to preserve. Both offer CRM-related capabilities. DealerSocket connects automotive CRM with a broader retail suite; we combine native customer records, opportunities and tasks with configured AI conversations and follow-up.


The decision may be replacement, a department-specific workspace or using the products together. Start with the[dealership AI buying guide](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/pillars/dealership-ai-buying-guide) and name the workflows before comparing features.


## Our CRM vs DealerSocket at a glance


Reviewed **October 26, 2026** , using official product sources and our current capabilities. We publish this comparison. Published capabilities do not establish that every module or integration is included in a quote.


Requirement DealerSocket Clearline (our platform)


CRM work Automotive customer and lead workflows, communication and reporting Native contacts, vehicles, opportunities, configurable pipelines and linked tasks


AI and communication Current Solera CRM pages describe AI lead response, scoring and coaching Customer conversations and configured outreach; separately enabled booking and inventory jobs


Retail scope Connected desking, digital retail and RevenueRadar offerings Check retained desking, equity and retail requirements; our capabilities do not establish an equivalent for every product


Staff ownership Demonstrate the selected product’s lead/task assignment and views Documented tasks with assignee, due date, department, priority and status; opportunity and task views


DMS connection Confirm records, directions and fees for the selected products and DMS PBS has documented object-specific directions and booking prerequisites; verify any other system separately


Deployment Evaluate the CRM and surrounding products your dealership will use Native CRM workspace, department-specific use or alongside deployment after requirement review


DealerSocket scope comes from[CRM by Solera](https://www.dealer.solera.com/products/dealersocket/crm/) and its[desking](https://dealersocket.com/products/crm/sales/desking/) and[RevenueRadar](https://www.dealer.solera.com/products/dealersocket/revenue-radar/) pages. Our[CRM](https://www.useclearline.com/product/crm) brings contacts, opportunities and tasks together, with separately configured AI actions.


## What DealerSocket’s broader scope means


DealerSocket’s automotive CRM and connected offerings cover more than customer messages. Desking and equity/lifecycle tools may be material requirements for the dealership’s sales process. Identify the selected products and how staff use them today.


If the buying brief includes constructing deals or finding equity opportunities, test those functions explicitly. Do not assume a conversation platform replaces them. Likewise, do not describe DealerSocket as a CRM without current AI when its official pages list AI capabilities.


Ask which features are included, which require another Solera product and what system data they use. A provider’s broad catalogue is not the same as the dealership’s proposed package.


## What our native CRM adds


Our[CRM](https://www.useclearline.com/product/crm) includes customer records with related vehicles, opportunities, conversations, tasks and meetings. Staff can configure pipelines and stages, work in board/table views and create owned follow-up with due dates and statuses.


That is a customer workspace your team can use, not just a place to read transcripts beside another CRM. You configure our AI communication and appointment actions separately. Read the[AI dealership CRM guide](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/ai-crm-car-dealership) for the operating walkthrough.


Whether it replaces a particular CRM depends on required desking, OEM lead handling, equity products, permissions, reports, imports, exports and integration behavior. Agree on that scope before promising replacement or migration timing.


## Run three matching demonstrations


### A sales lead that replies late


Create a test customer and vehicle, open the opportunity, choose a stage and assign the owner. Send an approved first response, then simulate a reply after that owner changes.


Inspect who sees the reply, where the conversation appears, how the next task is assigned and what stops conflicting outreach. Ask each vendor to separate automatic updates from staff actions.


### A service appointment that changes


Use the same service request with both products. Book a valid time, then reschedule and cancel it. Inspect the appointment after each action and confirm the receiving team’s context.


Our[PBS integration](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/clearline-pbs-systems-integration) requires contacts and vehicles two-way for two-way service appointments, plus a selected service calendar and OP-code mappings. Workplan events, tasks/reminders and appointments are pull-only. Do not assume a task in our CRM becomes a PBS Workplan task.


### A retail requirement you cannot lose


Choose a real requirement such as desking, an equity audience or an OEM workflow. Have DealerSocket show the selected product and ask us to identify how the requirement is covered or which retained tool is needed.


If you use an externally identified lease or service audience for outreach through our platform, demonstrate its source and available fields. Running a configured campaign is different from calculating equity or independently discovering an audience.


## When each deployment makes sense


**Evaluate DealerSocket** when the store wants automotive CRM tied to its required retail, desking and equity products. Test the included AI and the actual package rather than treating the suite as uniform.


**Evaluate our platform** when your buying brief centers on a native customer/opportunity workspace, owned tasks, conversations and configured AI actions across departments. Validate the requirements another system must retain.


**Use both with clear ownership** when DealerSocket remains responsible for selected retail or CRM work and we handle a defined set of customer workflows. Document the owner of each customer record, opportunity, task, appointment and outreach sequence. Test how replies and stop conditions move between the systems.


## Compare the cost of the same job


There is no verified matching price comparison in this guide. Request quotes for the same stores, users, workflows, usage, integrations, implementation and contract terms. Include retail products that remain after a change.


Use the[CRM pricing worksheet](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/automotive-crm-pricing) and[vendor acceptance scorecard](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/how-to-evaluate-dealership-ai-vendors) . Keep unresolved requirements visible rather than selecting a product on the lowest headline fee.


[See our CRM](https://www.useclearline.com/product/crm) and[bring the matching scenarios to a demo](https://www.useclearline.com/demo) . Ask the staff member who will use it to manage the opportunity and next task, then verify the connected-system result.


## Frequently asked questions


Is your platform only an add-on to DealerSocket? +


We provide native contacts, vehicles, opportunities, pipelines and tasks. You can also use our platform alongside existing tools. The appropriate deployment depends on the store’s required CRM, retail and integration scope.


Do you replace DealerSocket desking and RevenueRadar? +


Our current CRM and AI capabilities do not establish equivalent replacements for every DealerSocket retail or equity product. Test those requirements and identify retained tools before deciding.


Does DealerSocket have AI features? +


Its current Solera CRM pages list AI lead response, scoring and coaching. Confirm the capabilities and product inclusion in the dealership’s proposed package.


Can the two products work together? +


An alongside evaluation needs a verified integration scope and clear record/outreach ownership. Demonstrate replies, assignments, appointments, failed actions and stop conditions on the actual setup.
